title: OKR Delivery Spine: Initiative Commitment Levels, Failure Modes & Recovery Runbook
creator: Anika Rao
description: Purpose: Create a pragmatic, operational playbook that translates company-level OKRs into explicit initiative commitments, defines commitment levels (Gold/Silver/Bronze), enumerates likely failure modes, and prescribes recovery actions and escalation paths. Scope: company-wide OKRs and all cross-functional initiatives that span two or more teams (Engineering, Product, Design, Sales, Customer Success, Security). Excludes single-team technical debt tickets. Rationale: Current OKR handoffs are ambiguous; teams interpret commitment differently which leads to missed outcomes or late escalations. This spine standardizes expectations and reduces coordination overhead.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Commitment levels (Gold/Silver/Bronze) are defined with measurable criteria and example tradeoffs
A2: Failure modes matrix covering at least 6 common failure categories (resourcing, tech debt, infra, vendor, data quality, regulatory) is published
A3: Recovery runbook with step-by-step actions and owners for each failure mode is documented
A4: Escalation matrix with SLAs (24h, 72h, 7d) for Canary/Production/regression impacts is agreed and signed off by Eng and PM leadership
A5: Confluence page created and linked from company OKR hub; one training session delivered to all IC PMs and TPMs before Q2 planning closes

decisions: D1: Use three commitment levels to balance ambition and predictability (Gold: committed SLA + outcome; Silver: committed outcome w/ flexible scope; Bronze: exploratory/investigative)
D2: Recovery SLOs will be tracked in Console under a new ‘Initiative Health’ dashboard and will be a gating signal for rollouts
D3: Escalation cadence: 24h operational ticket -> 72h leadership sync -> 7d exec escalation if unresolved
rollout_plan: Week 1: finalize playbook and produce 1-pager; Week 2: leadership signoff and Confluence publish; Week 3: small cohort training (TPMs + PMs + Eng leads); Week 4: add Initiative Health widgets to Console and pilot on three cross-functional initiatives; Q2 planning: require commitment level selection for every company-level initiative.
risk_assessment: Primary risks: inconsistent adoption across org, over-prescription leading to slower decision-making, and missing instrumentation to detect failure modes. Mitigations: lightweight templates, pilot with three initiatives, automation of health signals in Console.
